doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: Closing thoughts: students' discoveries and learning from bandleaders
summary: Vega says he is happy, tells of a student crying at a breakthrough, criticizes shortcut careers, and credits Ray Barretto, Mongo and Tito Puente for tough lessons.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well this has been a very upbeat chat, Ray.

Yeah, man. And I’m a happy person. Some folks might perceive some of the things that I say as like oh he’s just dark. No, no, no. no. I love the music and I love to watch — I’ll tell you something I enjoy being in the moment of discovery when I’m playing but to watch my students have a moment of discovery in their lessons or on the bandstand when I’m playing with them, that’s worth a million dollars. I had a student in my class, my jazz trumpet student, and he put the horn down and he started to cry. And I went, “What’s happening, man?” He says, “I didn’t know I could do that.” I went, “Well you just did it.” He played through something like “Lady Bird” or something, which is the most — you know I gave him some concepts of how to play through it with rhythm and stuff like that and he played a nice solo on it. I went, “You played all the changes.” And he was like, “I didn’t know I could do this.” I went, “Yeah.” I said, “You’re a human being just like I am.” So yeah. Anyway I love all of the — I’m not a hater or anything and when I talk about the young generation of players coming up, they’re going to have to figure it out. Then again maybe I have to figure out what the new thing is because it’s completely changed. It’s all about — it’s about media presence and putting all sorts of stuff on line on a daily — content creation. That seems to be the way that people get record deals and — what’s the word, tours etcetera without having paid any dues with an older musician that’s going to tell them — excuse the French — “Yo that’s some sad shit, you’re not doing that here.” Okay?

I got that from Ray Barretto, from Mongo, from Tito Puente, oh my God, they read me the riot act. It wasn’t going to be a walk in the park. And from all the — my thing was learn from the bandleaders. Shut your mouth and learn from the older cats. Because they’re there. You know? So I don’t know — how did this one go? You know? Next time we have to have all three dogs. So this is Mitzy and then this is Ella.
